name: United Kingdom
instrument: Level 2 BIM mandate (2016, from the 2011 Government Construction Strategy); enforced in public procurement via The Construction Playbook (UK BIM Framework / BS EN ISO 19650)
authority: Cabinet Office; Infrastructure and Projects Authority (IPA)
effective: Level 2 BIM mandatory for central-government projects since April 2016; UK BIM Framework required for public works on a 'comply or explain' basis
summary: More than a roadmap. Collaborative (Level 2) BIM has been required on all centrally-procured central-government projects since April 2016, and the Construction Playbook obliges central departments and their arm's-length bodies — on a 'comply or explain' basis — to apply the UK BIM Framework (BS EN ISO 19650) in how public works are procured and delivered; the IPA's Transforming Infrastructure Performance roadmap carries it forward.
ifc_standards: BS EN ISO 16739 (IFC schema); ISO 19650 process; IFC not mandated for exchange
qualification_scheme: Digital Engineering Technician occupational standard (ST0266); RICS / BSI ISO 19650 individual certification

name: Italy
instrument: Decreto Ministeriale n. 560/2017 (Decreto BIM), amended by DM 312/2021
authority: Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti (MIT)
effective: Phased from 1 Jan 2019 (works ≥ €100M), cascading to public works ≥ €1M from 2025
summary: Progressive mandatory introduction of electronic modelling methods (BIM) by contracting authorities and operators across design, construction and management of public works, starting with the highest-value contracts.
ifc_standards: UNI EN ISO 16739 (IFC); UNI 11337; ISO 19650 process
qualification_scheme: UNI 11337-7 BIM roles; ICMQ certification (Accredia, UNI/PdR 78)

name: Spain
instrument: Orden PCM/818/2023 — Plan BIM en la contratación pública de la AGE
authority: Comisión Interministerial BIM (CIBIM) / Ministerio de la Presidencia
effective: Mandate since 2016 (tenders > €2M from 2018); Plan BIM 2023 phases adoption 2024–2030
summary: Establishes a mandatory BIM requirement in certain public contracts of the General State Administration and dependent bodies, on a progressive calendar designed to protect SME access.
ifc_standards: UNE-EN ISO 16739 (IFC); openBIM required in public procurement (Plan BIM)
qualification_scheme: buildingSMART Spain Professional Certification (Foundation / Practitioner)

name: Ireland
instrument: BIM requirements in the Capital Works Management Framework (CWMF)
authority: Office of Government Procurement
effective: From January 2024; phased by value, full coverage of public works by ~2028
summary: Public works contracts incorporate BIM via the CWMF, beginning with the highest-value projects and extending to design teams and contractors at progressively lower thresholds; aligned with ISO 19650.
ifc_standards: I.S. EN ISO 16739 (IFC); ISO 19650 (CWMF)
qualification_scheme: buildingSMART UK & Ireland certification; RICS / CIOB

name: Finland
instrument: Decree 751/2023 on information management in public construction
authority: Finnish Government (Ympäristöministeriö)
effective: In force from January 2025
summary: Legal requirement for digital design and information management in public construction commissioned by state authorities, requiring BIM-based, machine-readable documentation and lifecycle data handovers.

qualification_scheme: buildingSMART Nordic Professional Certification

name: Denmark
instrument: Bekendtgørelse nr. 118 af 06/02/2013 (ICT requirements in public construction)
authority: Bygningsstyrelsen (Danish Building & Property Agency)
effective: 2013 (building on 'Det Digitale Byggeri' since 2007)
summary: ICT/BIM requirements — object-based digital models, digital tendering and handover — are legally required for public construction above value thresholds (≈ DKK 5M state-funded; DKK 20M municipal/regional).
ifc_standards: DS/EN ISO 16739 (IFC); IFC exchange required under ICT regulations
qualification_scheme: buildingSMART Nordic Professional Certification

name: Lithuania

authority: Lietuvos Respublikos aplinkos ministerija (Ministry of Environment)
effective: In force from 25 Feb 2022; thresholds ≥ €5M (buildings) / €10M (engineering structures)
summary: Public-sector contracting authorities must include mandatory BIM requirements in procurement documents for design and works on special-category buildings ≥ €5M and engineering structures ≥ €10M.
ifc_standards: LST EN ISO 16739 (IFC); ISO 19650 owner information requirements
qualification_scheme: University / vocational BIM training; no national scheme

name: Russia
instrument: Town Planning Code Art. 57.5 (information model); Government Decrees No. 1431/2020 and No. 331/2021
authority: Government of the Russian Federation (Minstroy)
effective: Mandatory for budget-funded objects from 1 Jan 2022; extended to residential developers 2024–2025
summary: The Town Planning Code (Art. 57.5, introduced by Federal Law 151-FZ) establishes the legal concept of the construction information model; Decree No. 1431 sets the rules for forming and maintaining it, and Decree No. 331 made information modelling (TIM) mandatory for capital-construction objects financed from the budget system — later extended to residential developers.
ifc_standards: ГОСТ Р 10.0.02-2019 = ISO 16739:2018 (identical IFC schema); IFC required for exchange with expertise / state construction-supervision authorities; Minstroy XML schema builds on it; СП 333 is a code of practice, not a schema
qualification_scheme: Profstandard «Специалист в сфере ИМ в строительстве» (Минтруд №562н/2024); independent qualification assessment (НОК, FZ-238)

name: France
instrument: Plan BIM (and predecessors PTNB / Plan BIM 2022)
authority: Ministère de la Transition écologique
effective: Programme since 2015; voluntary by design
summary: France deliberately chose a voluntary, support-and-awareness approach rather than a legal mandate; individual public buyers may require BIM case-by-case, but there is no national obligation.

qualification_scheme: RNCP state title 'Coordinateur BIM'; buildingSMART (Mediaconstruct) certification

authority: Bundesministerium für Verkehr (BMV)
effective: BIM as standard for new federal transport infrastructure from 2020
summary: No general statutory mandate across all public construction, but BIM is the required standard for newly planned federal transport infrastructure (roads, rail, waterways) under the Stufenplan roadmap.

qualification_scheme: VDI/bS 2552 Blatt 8 qualification levels; buildingSMART Deutschland + VDI certification

name: Czech Republic
instrument: Act No. 330/2025 Sb. — Zákon o BIM (Act on management of information about construction and the built environment)
authority: Ministerstvo průmyslu a obchodu (MPO); Česká agentura pro standardizaci (ČAS)
effective: Adopted 2025 (330/2025 Sb.); mandatory building information model for above-threshold public works (≈ CZK 135M) from 1 Jan 2027; built-environment model from 2030; some information containers from 2032
summary: The adopted BIM Act (Act No. 330/2025 Sb., signed July 2025) makes a building information model mandatory for above-threshold (nadlimitní, ≈ CZK 135M) public works contracts and their design, procured by the state (its organisational units and subordinate bodies) and the regions and their organisations, with defined exceptions. The Act takes effect on 1 January 2027 (built-environment model from 2030; certain information containers from 2032), replacing the earlier voluntary concept.
ifc_standards: ČSN EN ISO 16739 (IFC); national data standard (DSS) under the BIM Act 330/2025 Sb.
qualification_scheme: BIM qualification in the National Qualifications System (Národní soustava kvalifikací); czBIM certification

name: Poland
instrument: BIM roadmap for public procurement (Ministry of Development and Technology)
authority: Ministerstwo Rozwoju i Technologii
effective: Roadmap 2020; BIM mandatory for public projects > €410M from 2025, all public projects by 2030
summary: Following the 2020 roadmap, BIM became mandatory for the largest public projects (over €410M) from 2025, with the requirement set to extend to all public projects by 2030; IFC delivery is expected in public procurement.
ifc_standards: PN-EN ISO 16739 (IFC); IFC required in public procurement
qualification_scheme: BIM training via providers; no official occupational standard

name: Estonia
instrument: Declaration of Intent on Digital Construction + BIM-based e-permitting
authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
effective: Declaration 2017; IFC-model building-permit submission available from 2024
summary: No national legal mandate; a voluntary inter-agency declaration drives adoption, and the state e-construction platform now accepts open IFC BIM models for building permits.
ifc_standards: EVS-EN ISO 16739 (IFC); IFC-based building-permit submission
qualification_scheme: University / vocational BIM training

name: United States
instrument: GSA agency requirement (model-based design + IFC); binding state mandates — WI, TX, OH, GA, MA
authority: U.S. General Services Administration (GSA); state facilities agencies; NIBS (standard)
effective: GSA requires native + IFC deliverables; states require BIM for state-funded buildings above value thresholds
summary: No federal BIM law. Much US activity is program and guidance — the GSA BIM Guides and the consensus National BIM Standard-US (NBIMS-US, NIBS). Binding requirements exist at two levels: the GSA requires model-based design with native + IFC deliverables on its federal projects, and five states mandate BIM for their own state-funded buildings — Wisconsin (first, 2009; now > $15M new / > $3M tenant-improvement), Texas (TFC), Ohio (OFCC), Georgia (GSFIC) and Massachusetts (DCAMM, ≥ $1M). Others publish BIM guidelines only (e.g. New York, Tennessee, Florida), and several DOTs (TxDOT, Caltrans, Iowa) mandate digital delivery for transport infrastructure; most states have no requirement.
ifc_standards: IFC (ISO 16739) via NBIMS-US; GSA & AASHTO require IFC; no single national adoption
qualification_scheme: AGC CM-BIM certificate; buildingSMART USA (BIMForum)

name: Brazil
instrument: Decreto nº 10.306/2020 (Estratégia BIM BR)
authority: Presidência da República (federal decree)
effective: Phase 1 from 1 Jan 2021; Phase 2 from 2024; Phase 3 from 2028
summary: Mandates BIM in the execution of engineering works and services by federal public administration bodies, rolled out in three phases from design modelling through to lifecycle asset management.

qualification_scheme: buildingSMART (BIM Fórum Brasil) Foundation certification

authority: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF)

summary: Approves the progressive, obligatory incorporation of BIM into public investment for entities under the national public-investment system, on a phased adoption timeline managed by the MEF.
ifc_standards: Plan BIM Perú; standards in development
qualification_scheme: Plan BIM Perú roles / competencies; no personal certification

summary: Plan BIM sets a national standard for public projects; BIM is required in Ministry of Public Works (MOP) tenders under that standard, while it remains optional for some other public bodies.

authority: Building and Construction Authority (BCA)

BIM e-submission applies to projects with GFA ≥ 5,000 m²; CORENET X submission is mandatory for new projects ≥ 30,000 m² from 1 October 2025 and for all new projects from 1 October 2026.

authority: Development Bureau (DEVB)
effective: Effective 1 Jan 2021, for tenders invited on/after that date

authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT)
effective: From FY2023, applied in principle to MLIT-directed public works (except small-scale)
summary: BIM/CIM is required in principle on MLIT directly-managed civil-works projects from FY2023 — 3D model deliverables, model-based design review and construction planning — with a hybrid IFC + PDF submission framework.

authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT)

summary: MOLIT guidelines apply BIM across construction sectors, with phased mandatory application beginning in public housing and integrated design-build projects, expanding to private buildings later in the decade.
ifc_standards: IFC required by agencies (PPS, LH); KBIMS; ISO 19650

authority: Prime Minister of Vietnam / Ministry of Construction
effective: From 2023 for grade-I/special-grade works; from 2025 for grade-II and above
summary: Prime Minister's roadmap mandates BIM for grade-I and special-grade construction works using public investment or state capital from 2023, extending to grade-II-and-above works from 2025.

qualification_scheme: buildingSMART Benelux Professional Certification

instrument: Federal building bodies (KBOB) BIM requirements; armasuisse & SBB adopt BIM from 2025; federal EMBAG 'open by default' law (in force 2024)
authority: KBOB; armasuisse Immobilien; SBB (federal railways); Confederation (EMBAG)
effective: Major federal projects (armasuisse Immobilien) and SBB phase BIM in from 2025; EMBAG in force 1 Jan 2024
summary: No BIM-specific national mandate and no single BIM regulator. The federal building and property bodies — coordinated via KBOB (armasuisse Immobilien, BBL, ETH-Rat, ASTRA) — apply BIM on major federal projects from 2025, and the federal railway SBB is phasing BIM in from 2025 (agency/owner-level requirements). Underpinning this, the federal EMBAG law (in force 1 Jan 2024) sets an 'open by default' principle for authorities — open-source software (Art. 9) and open government data (Art. 10) — which reinforces an open-standards / openBIM (IFC) approach across federal bodies, though EMBAG does not itself name BIM.
ifc_standards: SN EN ISO 16739 (IFC); SIA 2051; KBOB; federal 'open by default' law (EMBAG, 2024)
qualification_scheme: buildingSMART Switzerland (Bauen digital Schweiz) certification
